platform_info: The common set every organization builds on: gears, tools and SDKs from the platform's Gears repository, micro-frontends from FrontX and kits, synced once for all organizations, with crates.io adding published versions. A field you edit is kept as your organization's annotation, over the platform's facts. A gear an organization publishes joins this set once the platform merges it.
organization_info: What the organization builds, one row each: what its projects declare (a gear.toml or gear.gdl, a #[toolkit::gear] attribute, a FrontX package or a kit manifest), the code that could become a gear, and what it has published. Read from every project on a schedule, after a push, or now.
organization_info_members: Seen only by the organization's members; publishing one gives it to the platform, whose common set is one level up, under Platform.
repositories_sync_title: What the platform's components come from: what the catalogue lists and what products are built from
truncated: Showing the first {count} components. A marked type has more nodes than this page will render — narrow it on Objects, or filter above.
no_components_body: A platform administrator picks the repositories under Repositories, and syncs.
sources_description: Where the next sync reads the organization's catalogue from. This browser keeps the choice; the server keeps the repositories too, so the scheduled sync reads the same ones.
src_gears_note: Gears, tools, SDKs and plugins from the Gears repository.
src_frontx_note: Every package in a FrontX repository, wherever it sits, and every micro-frontend under src-app/mfe_packages/ with its mfe.json screens.
src_kits_note: Every .cf-studio-kit.toml in the repository — one at the root, or several in subdirectories. A kit is installed into a project's repositories rather than depended on, so it carries a repository and a ref instead of a version ladder.
src_kits_pm_note: One repository, several kits: its root manifest carries a [[kits]] entry each, so the scan finds whatever has been added since.
src_crates_note: Published versions, downloads and release dates.
no_tenant_for_connections: — no organization in context to list connections.
empty_view_note: The state a component page starts in — every cell a question.
fields_answered: {filled} of {total} fields answered · {derivable} derivable from the repository
no_schema_for_type: Nothing describes this component's type yet: no field schema.
spec_to_code_note: lines of code per line of spec
no_snapshot_body: The catalogue keeps one snapshot of each component a day, on every sync. None of this one is from the window yet, so there is nothing to compare with.
profile_help: The profile is Studio-owned and survives the crates.io sync. Put per-field answers under values, keyed by schema field id (e.g. owner, coverage), each a { v, b, n, s, l, u } object — s is the lamp (good/watch/bad), l a link, u a YYYY-MM-DD date. Optional diagram and uml blocks describe the architecture.
no_registry: This backend has no component registry yet (ADR-0041).
declared_many: {count} declared in more than one repository
decide_title: Code that could become a gear: declare it or reject it
decide_title_orphaned: {candidates} could become a gear; {orphaned} no repository declares any more
projects_read_hint: Every project is read unless it is excluded here: a registry with gaps nobody chose is what this page is for.
no_walk_yet: No project has been read yet.
nothing_read_body: Read the projects now, or wait for the schedule.
declared_many_title: Declared in more than one repository
orphaned_title: No repository declares it any more
published_no_project: Published, and no project of the organization declares it: it is read from the organization's repositories.
no_candidates: No candidates: nothing in the projects' code looks like a gear that is not declared one.
candidates_hint: Modules and crates that look like gears — their own REST surface, tables, types, a port or an SDK, other code using them, copies in other projects — and are not declared one. Strongest first.
score_title: The sum of its evidence's weights
merged_into: Merged into {name}: what is found under this name is recorded there.
published_once_platform: published once the platform's catalogue has it
pr_into_gear_repo: pull request into the gear repository
declare_done: Pull request opened on {branch} in {repo}. Once it is merged, the registry reads it as declared.
declare_preview: A pull request on {branch} in {repo} adds its manifest beside {path}:
publication_requested_note: Publication requested: waiting for a platform curator to publish it into the platform's gear repository, or to decline it.
request_publication_explain: Asks the platform to take this gear. A platform curator reviews the request, then opens a pull request into the platform's gear repository with its files, or declines it with a reason. The entry is published once the platform's catalogue has it.
reject_reason_placeholder: required: why this is not a gear
no_decisions_declared: None yet: found by the walk, nobody has decided.
suggest_hint: asks a model on your own key; nothing changes until you apply it
readiness_hint: reads its code and says what would stop it building as a crate of its own
outside_read: read {read} of the crate's {total} other files
extract_hint: moves it into the organization's gear repository as its own crate, with a pull request on each side
complete_hint: checks both pull requests are merged, tags the version, and marks it extracted
publications_info: Gears organizations ask the platform to take. A platform curator publishes one — a pull request into the platform's gear repository — or declines it with a reason. Once the platform's catalogue has it, it is in every organization's common set.
publications_refused_body: Only a platform administrator or a platform gear curator answers them.
no_open_requests_body: An organization asks from its gear's row; the request lands here.
publish_title: Open the pull request into the platform's gear repository
decline_reason_placeholder: required: why the platform does not take it
cannot_preview: This backend cannot preview a publish.
curators_info: People who answer publication requests beside the platform's administrators (the platform-gear-curator role). Only a platform administrator changes this list.
no_curators_body: The platform's administrators answer every request.
repositories_info: Where the platform's components come from: the repositories the platform's catalogue reads, and the crates.io keyword that adds published versions. Every organization's catalogue reads them.
platform_sources_admin_only: Only a platform administrator sees and changes the platform's sources.
platform_sources_admin_only_body: What they read is under Platform › Components.
platform_sources_note: What the platform's catalogue reads — the shared components every organization sees under Platform. Only a platform administrator sees and changes this.
platform_saved: Saved. The platform's catalogue is synced daily from these.
